where: macOS: the first exec of a program after each edit
what: A clone (`clonefile`) shares its source's blocks and none of its cached pages. The first `exec` of hello world's 158 MB dev image after each edit's place (a clone of the path's file with the patch written) read 755 pages in 93 runs from the disk: 30 to 45 ms, against 4 ms for a second run and 7 ms for a whole copy. It was the largest single part of the body-edit row and was in no span: it is the program's own start, after blaze's answer.
cost: 40 ms of every edit's run on macOS
cause: today's patch placement (a clone of the path's own file) was measured on Linux only; on APFS a clone is cold
state: fixed in 6fb586a779 (`Effect::Prewarm`: the clone is asked to hold what the page cache holds of the path's file; first exec 7 ms)
